When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

# 项目学习手册·单篇讲义生成 Worker

## 角色

你是资深技术教育专家、源码阅读导师和代码实践教练。

你运行在被分析项目的根目录内。

你可以使用：

- `Read`
- `Grep`
- `Glob`
- 只读 `git` 命令，例如 `git log`、`git diff`、`git show`、`git ls-files`

你可以写文件，但只能写入：

- `<项目名>-tutorial/`

你只能生成 stdin 指定的那一篇讲义。

禁止：

- 修改源码。
- 生成其他讲义。
- 修改 manifest。
- 写入讲义目录之外的文件。

---

## 总目标

根据 stdin 中给出的讲义规格，生成一篇适合学习手册的 Markdown 讲义。

讲义必须：

1. 全部使用中文。
2. 从零开始解释，不默认读者已经熟悉项目。
3. 结合真实源码讲解。
4. 包含可操作的代码实践任务。
5. 结构清晰，适合长期维护。
6. 对关键源码给出永久链接和行号。
7. 不编造不存在的代码、命令、接口或行为。

---

## 工作流程

生成讲义前，请按顺序完成：

1. 阅读 stdin 中的讲义规格。
2. 阅读 `source_files` 中列出的关键源码。
3. 如果源码不足，用 `Grep` / `Glob` 补充查找相关入口、测试、示例和调用链。
4. 确认本讲义的最小模块。
5. 根据 action 执行：

   - `new`：从零创建该讲义。
   - `rebuild`：从零重建该讲义。
   - `update`：先读取已有讲义，再结合 diff 更新。
   - `keep`：如果被调用，通常不需要编辑文件，只做简短说明。

---

## update 模式规则

当 action 为 `update` 时：

1. 先 `Read` 当前已有的讲义文件。
2. 使用 `git diff previous_head..current_head` 查看相关代码变化。
3. 更新已经失效的源码说明。
4. 刷新所有永久链接中的 head 和行号。
5. 保留仍然正确的内容。
6. 新增必要解释和实践步骤。
7. 如果核心流程已经变化，可以重写受影响章节。

---

## 讲义标准结构

每篇讲义必须使用下面的结构。

```md
# 讲义标题

## 1. 本讲目标

说明读者学完后应该掌握什么。

## 2. 前置知识

用通俗语言解释本讲需要的基础概念。

## 3. 本讲源码地图

列出本讲涉及的关键文件，并说明每个文件的作用。

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

按最小模块拆分。

每个最小模块都必须包含：

### 4.x 模块名称

#### 4.x.1 概念说明

解释这个模块是什么、解决什么问题、为什么需要它。

#### 4.x.2 核心流程

用列表、流程图式文字或伪代码描述执行过程。

如涉及算法、协议、并发、缓存、调度、状态机等，可以补充必要数学或原理说明。

数学公式使用：

- 行内：\( ... \)
- 独立公式：\[ ... \]

不要使用 `$...$`。

#### 4.x.3 源码精读

引用真实项目代码。

每个关键代码点都要给出永久链接，格式为：

[文件路径:L起始-L结束](<permalink_base>/<相对路径>#L起始-L结束)

链接旁边必须用中文说明这段代码做了什么。

#### 4.x.4 代码实践

给出一个可操作的小实践，例如：

- 运行一个示例。
- 阅读一个测试。
- 修改一个配置。
- 添加一行日志。
- 改一个参数观察行为。
- 编写一个最小调用示例。
- 跟踪一条调用链。

实践步骤要包含：

1. 实践目标。
2. 操作步骤。
3. 需要观察的现象。
4. 预期结果。
5. 如果无法确定运行结果，明确写「待本地验证」。

不要假装已经运行过命令。

#### 4.x.5 小练习与答案

给出 2 到 3 个练习题，并直接给出参考答案。
```

---

## 讲义结尾必须包含

```md
## 5. 综合实践

设计一个贯穿本讲主要内容的小任务，帮助读者把知识串起来。

## 6. 本讲小结

用 3 到 6 条 bullet 总结本讲。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

说明下一讲应该学习什么，或者建议读者继续阅读哪些源码。
```

---

## 代码实践要求

每篇讲义至少包含一个完整代码实践。

实践优先从以下位置寻找依据：

- README
- examples
- tests
- scripts
- package scripts
- Makefile
- CI 配置
- 项目已有 demo

如果找不到可运行示例，也必须提供「源码阅读型实践」，例如：

- 跟踪函数调用链。
- 根据测试断言理解行为。
- 修改局部参数并说明应该观察什么。
- 给关键函数添加日志。
- 阅读配置加载过程并画出流程。

---

## 源码引用要求

- 只引用实际存在的文件。
- 行号必须准确。
- 永久链接必须使用当前 HEAD。
- 如果无法确认行号，不要编造，标注「待确认」。
- 示例代码如果不是项目原有代码，必须明确标注为「示例代码」。

---

## 写作风格

- 中文。
- 深入浅出。
- 先讲直觉，再讲源码。
- 多使用标题、列表、表格和伪代码。
- 不要写空泛总结。
- 不要堆砌大段源码。
- 代码片段要短，只保留关键部分。
- 对初学者不熟悉的术语要解释。

---

## 输出与写入规则

- 只写 stdin 指定的文件。
- 文件路径必须是 `<项目名>-tutorial/<filename>`。
- 不要写其他文件。
- 不要修改源码。
- 完成后，用一句话总结本讲义覆盖了哪些最小模块。

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

run_in_background.description: Agents run in the background by default; you will be notified when one completes. Set to false only when your very next action depends on this agent's result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise leave it in the background so the user can hand you other work.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `find`, `grep`, `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 600000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. With it, `timeout` limits how long the command may run in the background before it is stopped (default 600000 ms, max 7200000 ms).

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

tools.name: Edit
tools.description:
Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>

schema.name: Workflow
schema.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

from pathlib import Path

import re

import requests

from sympy.parsing import sympy_parser as spp

from .ch02 import (

RE_NUMBER = re.compile(
    r"-?(?:\d+/\d+|\d+(?:\.\d+)?(?:[eE][+-]?\d+)?)"
)

LATEX_FIXES = [  # Latex formatting to be replaced
    (r"\\left\s*", ""),
    (r"\\right\s*", ""),
    (r"\\,|\\!|\\;|\\:", ""),
    (r"\\cdot", "*"),
    (r"\u00B7|\u00D7", "*"),
    (r"\\\^\\circ", ""),
    (r"\\dfrac", r"\\frac"),
    (r"\\tfrac", r"\\frac"),
    (r"°", ""),
]

RE_SPECIAL = re.compile(r"<\|[^>]+?\|>")  # strip chat special tokens like <|assistant|>
SUPERSCRIPT_MAP = {
    "⁰": "0", "¹": "1", "²": "2", "³": "3", "⁴": "4",
    "⁵": "5", "⁶": "6", "⁷": "7", "⁸": "8", "⁹": "9",
    "⁺": "+", "⁻": "-", "⁽": "(", "⁾": ")",
}


def load_model_and_tokenizer(which_model, device, use_compile, local_dir="qwen3"):
    if which_model == "base":

        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="base", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-base.json"
        model_path = Path(local_dir) / "qwen3-0.6B-base.pth"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path)

    elif which_model == "reasoning":

        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="reasoning", tokenizer_only=False, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-reasoning.json"
        model_path = Path(local_dir) / "qwen3-0.6B-reasoning.pth"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(
            tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path,
            apply_chat_template=True,
            add_generation_prompt=True,
            add_thinking=True,
        )

    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid choice: which_model={which_model}")

    model = Qwen3Model(QWEN_CONFIG_06_B)
    model.load_state_dict(torch.load(model_path))

    model.to(device)

    if use_compile:
        torch._dynamo.config.allow_unspec_int_on_nn_module = True
        model = torch.compile(model)

    return model, tokenizer


def load_tokenizer_only(which_model, local_dir="qwen3"):
    if which_model == "base":
        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="base", tokenizer_only=True, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-base.json"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path)

    elif which_model == "reasoning":
        download_qwen3_small(
            kind="reasoning", tokenizer_only=True, out_dir=local_dir
        )

        tokenizer_path = Path(local_dir) / "tokenizer-reasoning.json"
        tokenizer = Qwen3Tokenizer(
            tokenizer_file_path=tokenizer_path,
            apply_chat_template=True,
            add_generation_prompt=True,
            add_thinking=True,
        )

    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid choice: which_model={which_model}")

    return tokenizer


def generate_text_stream_concat(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device, max_new_tokens,
    verbose=False,
):
    input_ids = torch.tensor(
        tokenizer.encode(prompt), device=device
        ).unsqueeze(0)

    generated_ids = []
    for token in generate_text_basic_stream_cache(
        model=model,
        token_ids=input_ids,
        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
    ):
        next_token_id = token.squeeze(0)
        generated_ids.append(next_token_id.item())

        if verbose:
            print(
                tokenizer.decode(next_token_id.tolist()),
                end="",
                flush=True
            )
    return tokenizer.decode(generated_ids)

    boxed_start_idx = text.rfind(r"\boxed")

def render_prompt(prompt):
    template = (
        "You are a helpful math assistant.\n"
        "Answer the question and write the final result on a new line as:\n"
        "\\boxed{ANSWER}\n\n"
        f"Question:\n{prompt}\n\nAnswer:"
    )
    return template


def load_math500_test(local_path="math500_test.json", save_copy=True):
    local_path = Path(local_path)
    url = (
        "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/"
        "main/ch03/01_main-chapter-code/math500_test.json"
    )

    if local_path.exists():
        with local_path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            data = json.load(f)
    else:
        r = requests.get(url, timeout=30)
        r.raise_for_status()
        data = r.json()

        if save_copy:  # Saves a local copy
            with local_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(data, f, indent=2)

    return data


def mini_eval_demo(model, tokenizer, device):
    ex = {  # Test example with "problem" and "answer" fields
        "problem": "Compute 1/2 + 1/6.",
        "answer": "2/3"
    }
    prompt = render_prompt(ex["problem"])     # 1. Apply prompt template
    gen_text = generate_text_stream_concat(   # 2. Generate response
        model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
        max_new_tokens=64,
    )
    pred_answer = extract_final_candidate(gen_text)  # 3. Extract and normalize answer
    is_correct = grade_answer(                       # 4. Grade answer
        pred_answer, ex["answer"]
    )
    print(f"Device: {device}")
    print(f"Prediction: {pred_answer}")
    print(f"Ground truth: {ex['answer']}")
    print(f"Correct: {is_correct}")


def eta_progress_message(
    processed,
    total,
    start_time,
    show_eta=False,
    label="Progress",
):
    progress = f"{label}: {processed}/{total}"
    pad_width = len(f"{label}: {total}/{total} | ETA: 00h 00m 00s")
    if not show_eta or processed <= 0:
        return progress.ljust(pad_width)

    elapsed = time.time() - start_time
    if elapsed <= 0:
        return progress.ljust(pad_width)

    remaining = max(total - processed, 0)

    if processed:
        avg_time = elapsed / processed
        eta_seconds = avg_time * remaining
    else:
        eta_seconds = 0

    eta_seconds = max(int(round(eta_seconds)), 0)
    minutes, rem_seconds = divmod(eta_seconds, 60)
    hours, minutes = divmod(minutes, 60)
    if hours:
        eta = f"{hours}h {minutes:02d}m {rem_seconds:02d}s"
    elif minutes:
        eta = f"{minutes:02d}m {rem_seconds:02d}s"
    else:
        eta = f"{rem_seconds:02d}s"

    message = f"{progress} | ETA: {eta}"
    return message.ljust(pad_width)


def evaluate_math500_stream(
    model,
    tokenizer,
    device,
    math_data,
    out_path=None,
    max_new_tokens=512,
    verbose=False,
):

    if out_path is None:
        dev_name = str(device).replace(":", "-")  # Make filename compatible with Windows
        out_path = Path(f"math500-{dev_name}.jsonl")

    num_examples = len(math_data)
    num_correct = 0
    total_len = 0  # Calculates the average response length (see exercise 3.2)
    start_time = time.time()

    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:  # Save results for inspection
        for i, row in enumerate(math_data, start=1):
            prompt = render_prompt(row["problem"])    # 1. Apply prompt template
            gen_text = generate_text_stream_concat(   # 2. Generate response
                model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
                max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
                verbose=verbose,
            )
            total_len += len(tokenizer.encode(gen_text))

            extracted = extract_final_candidate(  # 3. Extract and normalize answer
                gen_text
            )
            is_correct = grade_answer(            # 4. Grade answer
                extracted, row["answer"]
            )
            num_correct += int(is_correct)

            record = {  # Record to be saved for inspection
                "index": i,
                "problem": row["problem"],
                "gtruth_answer": row["answer"],
                "generated_text": gen_text,
                "extracted": extracted,
                "correct": bool(is_correct),
            }
            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")

            progress_msg = eta_progress_message(
                processed=i,
                total=num_examples,

                show_eta=True,

markdown# Chapter 4: Improving Reasoning with Inference-Time Scaling markdownPackages that are being used in this notebook: from importlib.metadata import version used_libraries = [ "matplotlib", "reasoning_from_scratch", "torch", "tokenizers" # Used by reasoning_from_scratch ] for lib in used_libraries: print(f"{lib} version: {version(lib)}") matplotlib version: 3.10.8 reasoning_from_scratch version: 0.1.13 torch version: 2.9.1 tokenizers version: 0.22.2 markdown markdown  ## 4.1 Introduction to inference-time scaling markdown markdown- Plot above inspired by OpenAI o1 blog post, https://openai.com/index/learning-to-reason-with-llms/ markdown markdown- All 3 methods more than double the accuracy of the base model on MATH-500 (the benchmark from the prev. chapter) - Methods 1 and 2 are covered in this chapter; method 3 is covered in the next chapter markdown  ## 4.2 Loading a pre-trained model markdown- Model loading code similar to chapters 2 and 3 import torch from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import get_device from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import ( load_model_and_tokenizer ) device = get_device() # Use CPU for the first run of this chapter device = torch.device("cpu") model, tokenizer = load_model_and_tokenizer( which_model="base", device=device, use_compile=False ) Using Apple Silicon GPU (MPS) ✓ qwen3/qwen3-0.6B-base.pth already up-to-date markdown- Let's try the model on a prompt from the MATH-500 dataset, which we worked with in the previous chapter: from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import render_prompt raw_prompt = ( "Half the value of $3x-9$ is $x+37$. " "What is the value of $x$?" ) prompt = render_prompt(raw_prompt) print(prompt) You are a helpful math assistant. Answer the question and write the final result on a new line as: \boxed{ANSWER} Question: Half the value of $3x-9$ is $x+37$. What is the value of $x$? Answer: markdown- The following function is based on `generate_text_stream_concat` from the previous chapter, but we modify it slightly to be able to pass in other `generate_*` functions later from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import generate_text_basic_stream_cache def generate_text_stream_concat_flex( model, tokenizer, prompt, device, max_new_tokens, verbose=False, generate_func=None, # New **generate_kwargs # New ): if generate_func is None: # New generate_func = generate_text_basic_stream_cache input_ids = torch.tensor( tokenizer.encode(prompt), device=device ).unsqueeze(0) generated_ids = [] for token in generate_func( # New model=model, token_ids=input_ids, max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id, **generate_kwargs, # New ): next_token_id = token.squeeze(0) generated_ids.append(next_token_id.item()) if verbose: print( tokenizer.decode(next_token_id.tolist()), end="", flush=True ) return tokenizer.decode(generated_ids) response = generate_text_stream_concat_flex( model, tokenizer, prompt, device, max_new_tokens=2048, verbose=True, generate_func=generate_text_basic_stream_cache # NEW ) \boxed{20} markdown- By the way, the correct answer is 83 markdown  ## 4.3 Generating better responses with chain-of-thought prompting markdown- A classic way to improve model performance is to modify the prompt to encourage the model to think or explain step by step markdown prompt_cot = prompt + " \n\nExplain step by step." response_cot = generate_text_stream_concat_flex( model, tokenizer, prompt_cot, device, max_new_tokens=2048, verbose=True, ) To solve the problem, we need to find the value of \( x \) such that half the value of \( 3x - 9 \) is equal to \( x + 37 \). ### Step 1: Set up the equation We are given that half the value of \( 3x - 9 \) is equal to \( x + 37 \). This can be written as: \[ \frac{1}{2}(3x - 9) = x + 37 \] ### Step 2: Eliminate the fraction To eliminate the fraction, multiply both sides of the equation by 2: \[ 2 \cdot \frac{1}{2}(3x - 9) = 2(x + 37) \] Simplifying both sides: \[ 3x - 9 = 2x + 74 \] ### Step 3: Solve for \( x \) Subtract \( 2x \) from both sides to isolate \( x \): \[ 3x - 2x - 9 = 74 \] Simplify: \[ x - 9 = 74 \] Add 9 to both sides to solve for \( x \): \[ x = 74 + 9 \] \[ x = 83 \] ### Final Answer: \[ \boxed{83} \] markdown  ## 4.4 Controlling output diversity with temperature scaling markdown- So far, we have used deterministic decoding; this section introduces stochastic decoding - We start with temperature scaling, and later in section 4.5, we add top-p to balance randomness and coherence better markdown markdown  ### 4.4.1 Understanding the process of selecting the next token ex_prompt = "The capital of Germany is" response = generate_text_stream_concat_flex( model, tokenizer, ex_prompt, device, max_new_tokens=1, verbose=True ) Berlin markdown- What happens under the hood: markdown # 1) Convert input text into token IDs input_token_ids = torch.tensor( tokenizer.encode(ex_prompt), device=device ).unsqueeze(0) print(input_token_ids) tensor([[ 785, 6722, 315, 9856, 374]]) # 2) Get scores for next token with torch.inference_mode(): next_token_logits = model(input_token_ids)[:, -1] print(next_token_logits.shape) # Shape: [1, vocab_size] torch.Size([1, 151936]) # 3) Find vocabulary index with highest score max_token_id = torch.argmax(next_token_logits) print(f"Token ID: {max_token_id}") print(f"Decoded token: '{tokenizer.decode([max_token_id])}'") Token ID: 19846 Decoded token: ' Berlin' markdown- The LLM has a vocabulary size of 151,936 tokens with token indices 0 to 151,935; we only focus on a subset of 100 tokens between indices 19,800 and 19,900 (easier to visualize) import matplotlib.pyplot as plt def plot_scores_bar( next_token_logits, start=19_800, end=19_900, arrow=True, ylabel="Logit value" ): # Select vocabulary subsection x = torch.arange(start, end) # .cpu() is a shortcut for to(torch.device("cpu")) logits_section = next_token_logits[0, start:end].float().cpu() # Plot logits plt.bar(x, logits_section) plt.xlabel("Vocabulary index") plt.ylabel(ylabel) # Highlight max logit if arrow: max_idx = torch.argmax(logits_section) plt.annotate( "Berlin", xy=(x[max_idx], logits_section[max_idx]), xytext=(x[max_idx] - 25, logits_section[max_idx] - 2), arrowprops={ "facecolor": "black", "arrowstyle": "->", "lw": 1.5 }, fontsize=10, ) plt.grid(alpha=0.3) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() plot_scores_bar(next_token_logits) Outputs are too large to include. Use Bash with: cat | jq '.cells[34].outputs' markdown  ### 4.4.2 Rescaling token scores (logits) via a temperature parameter markdown def scale_logits_by_temperature(logits, temperature): if temperature <= 0: raise ValueError("Temperature must be positive") return logits / temperature markdown- Technically, it's better to use a bar plot, but lines make it easier to see the difference: def plot_logits_with_temperature( next_token_logits, start=19_800, end=19_900, temps=(0.5, 5.0), ): x = torch.arange(start, end) logits_orig = next_token_logits[0, start:end].float().cpu() # Apply temperature scaling logits_scaled = [ scale_logits_by_temperature(logits_orig, T) for T in temps ] # Plot logits plt.plot(x, logits_orig, label="Original logits", lw=2) plt.plot( x, logits_scaled[0], label=f"T={temps[0]} (sharper)", ls="--", lw=1 ) plt.plot( x, logits_scaled[1], label=f"T={temps[1]} (flatter)", ls=":", lw=3 ) # Highlight max logit max_idx = torch.argmax(logits_orig) plt.annotate( "Berlin", xy=(x[max_idx], logits_orig[max_idx]), xytext=(x[max_idx] - 25, logits_orig[max_idx] + 2), arrowprops={"facecolor": "black", "arrowstyle": "->", "lw": 1.5}, fontsize=12, ) plt.xlabel("Vocabulary index") plt.ylabel("Logit value") plt.legend() plt.grid(alpha=0.3) plt.tight_layout() plt.show() plot_logits_with_temperature( next_token_logits, temps=(0.5, 5.0) ) Outputs are too large to include. Step 3.4: Sample token according to probabilities torch.manual_seed(123) print( "Sampled token:", torch.multinomial(next_token_probas.cpu(), num_samples=1) ) Sampled token: tensor([[65094]]) print(tokenizer.decode([65094])) mistress def count_samples(probas, num_samples=1000, threshold=1, tokenizer=None): # Draw samples according to probabilities samples = torch.multinomial( probas.cpu(), num_samples=num_samples, replacement=True ) # Count how often each index was selected counts = torch.bincount(samples.squeeze(0), minlength=1) # Print results for i, c in enumerate(counts): if c > threshold: if tokenizer is None: print(f"Vocab index {i}: {c.item()}x") else: print(f"'{tokenizer.decode([i])}': {c.item()}x") torch.manual_seed(123) count_samples(next_token_probas, tokenizer=tokenizer) '}': 2x ' torch.manual_seed(123) probas_lowT = torch.softmax( scale_logits_by_temperature(next_token_logits, 0.35), dim=-1 ) count_samples(probas_lowT, threshold=1, tokenizer=tokenizer) ' __': 158x ' Berlin': 435x ' ____': 169x ' ______': 209x ' Munich': 3x ' Hamburg': 3x ' _____': 18x print(probas_lowT[0, 19_846]) tensor(0.4199, dtype=torch.bfloat16) markdown- The `"______"` is likely because the model likely has seen formatting like this in the training set and tries to generate a quiz for the user markdown  ### 4.4.4 Adding temperature scaling to the text generation function # from reasoning_from_scratch.ch02 import generate_text_basic_stream_cache


def generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device, max_new_tokens,
    verbose=False, 
    generate_func=None,  # New
    **generate_kwargs  # New
):

    if generate_func is None:  # New
        generate_func = generate_text_basic_stream_cache
        
    input_ids = torch.tensor(
        tokenizer.encode(prompt), device=device
        ).unsqueeze(0)

    generated_ids = []
    for token in generate_func(  # New
        model=model,
        token_ids=input_ids,
        max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens,
        eos_token_id=tokenizer.eos_token_id,
        **generate_kwargs,  # New
    ):
        next_token_id = token.squeeze(0)
        generated_ids.append(next_token_id.item())

        if verbose:
            print(
                tokenizer.decode(next_token_id.tolist()),
                end="",
                flush=True
            )
    return tokenizer.decode(generated_ids)

response = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
    max_new_tokens=2048, verbose=True,
    generate_func=generate_text_basic_stream_cache  # NEW
)

To solve the problem, we need to find the value of \( x \) such that half the value of \( 3x - 9 \) is equal to \( x + 37 \).

### Step 1: Set up the equation
We are given that half the value of \( 3x - 9 \) is equal to \( x + 37 \). This can be written as:
\[
\frac{1}{2}(3x - 9) = x + 37
\]

### Step 2: Eliminate the fraction
To eliminate the fraction, multiply both sides of the equation by 2:
\[
2 \cdot \frac{1}{2}(3x - 9) = 2(x + 37)
\]
Simplifying both sides:
\[
3x - 9 = 2x + 74
\]

### Step 3: Solve for \( x \)
Subtract \( 2x \) from both sides to isolate \( x \):
\[
3x - 2x - 9 = 74
\]
Simplify:
\[
x - 9 = 74
\]
Add 9 to both sides to solve for \( x \):
\[
x = 74 + 9
\]
\[
x = 83
\]

### Final Answer:
\[
\boxed{83}
\]

### 4.4.4 Adding temperature scaling to the text generation function

# Exercise 2.2 Appendix B
from reasoning_from_scratch.qwen3 import KVCache

@torch.inference_mode()
def generate_text_temp_stream_cache(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None,
    temperature=0.
):
    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])
    model.reset_kv_cache()

    # Step 3.1: Get logits
    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]
    for step in range(max_new_tokens):

        ########################################
        # NEW:
        orig_device = token_ids.device

        if temperature is None or temperature == 0.0:
            next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        else:
            # Step 3.2: Apply temperature scaling on logits
            logits = scale_logits_by_temperature(out, temperature)

            # Step 3.3: Convert to probabilities
            probas = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)

            # Step 3.4: Sample token according to probabilities
            next_token = torch.multinomial(probas.cpu(), num_samples=1)
            next_token = next_token.to(orig_device)
            
        #########################################
        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token
        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]

torch.manual_seed(123)

### 4.5.2 Adding a top-p filter to the text generation function

def top_p_filter(probas, top_p):
    if top_p is None or top_p >= 1.0:
        return probas

    # Step 4.1: Sort by descending probability
    sorted_probas, sorted_idx = torch.sort(probas, dim=1, descending=True)

    # Step 4.2: Cumulative sum
    cumprobas = torch.cumsum(sorted_probas, dim=1)

    # Step 4.3.1: Keep tokens where prefix cumulative mass (before token) is < top_p
    # Example: [0.5, 0.41, 0.09] with top_p=0.9 should keep the first two tokens
    prefix = cumprobas - sorted_probas   # cumulative mass before each token
    keep = prefix < top_p
    # Always keep at least one token (fallback for very small/non-positive top_p)
    keep[:, 0] = True    

    # Step 4.3.2: Zero out beyond cutoff
    kept_sorted = torch.where(
        keep, sorted_probas,
        torch.zeros_like(sorted_probas)
    )
    # Step 4.3.3: Map back to original order
    filtered = torch.zeros_like(probas).scatter(1, sorted_idx, kept_sorted)

    # Step 4.4: Renormalize to sum to 1
    denom = torch.sum(filtered, dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)
    return filtered / denom

def generate_text_top_p_stream_cache(
    model,
    token_ids,
    max_new_tokens,
    eos_token_id=None,
    temperature=0.,
    top_p=None
):
    model.eval()
    cache = KVCache(n_layers=model.cfg["n_layers"])
    model.reset_kv_cache()

    # Step 3.1: Get logits
    out = model(token_ids, cache=cache)[:, -1]
    for step in range(max_new_tokens):

        orig_device = token_ids.device

        if temperature is None or temperature == 0.0:
            next_token = torch.argmax(out, dim=-1, keepdim=True)

        else:
            # Step 3.2: Apply temperature scaling on logits
            logits = scale_logits_by_temperature(out, temperature)

            # Step 3.3: Convert to probabilities
            probas = torch.softmax(logits, dim=-1)

            # (New) Step 4: Apply top-p filter to probabilities
            probas = top_p_filter(probas, top_p)            

            # Step 3.4: Sample token according to probabilities
            next_token = torch.multinomial(probas.cpu(), num_samples=1)
            next_token = next_token.to(orig_device)

        if (eos_token_id is not None
                and torch.all(next_token == eos_token_id)):
            break

        yield next_token
        if step + 1 < max_new_tokens:  # Skips the forward pass after the last token is generated
            out = model(next_token, cache=cache)[:, -1]

torch.manual_seed(123)
response = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
    max_new_tokens=2048, verbose=True,
    generate_func=generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
    temperature=0.5,
    top_p=0.8,

## 4.6 Improving response accuracy with self-consistency
- Generate multiple answers (/reasoning chains) via sampling and vote

- Similar to classic majority voting, but instead of different models, use different temperature settings
- This method is also described in the [Self-Consistency Improves Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.11171) paper
- In short, this method
  - Samples multiple reasoning chains with high temperature and top-p
  - Extracts the final answer from each chain
  - Chooses the most frequent final answer
- Nit: this is called [plurality vote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plurality_(voting)) (in American English), not majority vote

from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import extract_final_candidate
from collections import Counter

def self_consistency_vote(
    model, tokenizer, prompt, device,
    num_samples=10, temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9, max_new_tokens=2048,
    show_progress=True, show_long_answer=False, seed=None,
):
    full_answers, short_answers = [], []

    # 1) Sample multiple answers
    for i in range(num_samples):
        if seed is not None:
            torch.manual_seed(seed + i + 1)

        answer = generate_text_stream_concat_flex(
            model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, prompt=prompt, device=device,
            max_new_tokens=max_new_tokens, verbose=show_long_answer,
            generate_func=generate_text_top_p_stream_cache,
            temperature=temperature, top_p=top_p,
        )

        # 2) Extract the final (short) answer from each answer
        short = extract_final_candidate(
            answer, fallback="number_then_full"
        )
        full_answers.append(answer)
        short_answers.append(short)
        if show_progress:
            print(f"[Sample {i+1}/{num_samples}] → {short!r}")

    # 3) Choose the most frequent final answer (self-consistency vote)
    counts = Counter(short_answers)
    groups = {s: [] for s in counts}
    for idx, s in enumerate(short_answers):
        groups[s].append(idx)

    mc = counts.most_common()
    if not mc:
        majority_winners, final_answer = [], None
    else:
        top_freq = mc[0][1]
        majority_winners = [s for s, f in mc if f == top_freq]
        final_answer = mc[0][0] if len(majority_winners) == 1 else None

    return {
        "full_answers": full_answers,
        "short_answers": short_answers,
        "counts": dict(counts),
        "groups": groups,
        "majority_winners": majority_winners,
        "final_answer": final_answer,
    }

- Additional tips
  - If all (long) answers look nearly identical, increase temperature gently to increase diversity  
  - If (long) answers look off, decrease temperature

To find the value of \( x \), let's solve the equation step by step.

1. **Given Equation:**
   \[
   \frac{1}{2} \times (3x - 9) = x + 37
   \]

2. **Multiply Both Sides by 2 to Eliminate the Fraction:**
   \[
   2 \times \frac{1}{2} \times (3x - 9) = 2 \times (x + 37)
   \]
   \[
   3x - 9 = 2x + 74
   \]

3. **Subtract \( 2x \) from Both Sides to Get:**
   \[
   3x - 2x - 9 = 74
   \]
   \[
   x - 9 = 74
   \]

4. **Add 9 to Both Sides to Solve for \( x \):**
   \[
   x = 74 + 9
   \]
   \[
   x = 83
   \]

\[
\boxed{83}
\]

41	### 4.1 top_p_filter：五步流水线
42	
43	#### 4.1.1 概念说明
44	
45	`top_p_filter` 解决的问题：**在概率分布上动态划一条截止线，把长尾「核外」token 的概率清零，再把剩余质量重归一化为合法分布**，供后续 `torch.multinomial` 采样。
46	
47	它和温度的分工可以用一句话概括：
48	
49	> **温度负责「重塑」整个分布的形状，top-p 负责「砍掉」分布的尾巴。** 温度再怎么调，每个 token 的概率都还是正数；top-p 之后，核外 token 的概率严格为 0，永远不可能被采到。
50	
51	为什么要砍尾巴？实践中发现（这正是原论文标题 "The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration" 指出的现象）：语言模型分布的长尾里堆满了语料中「偶尔出现过」的低质拼接，人类文本从来不会从均匀的全词表里选词。砍掉长尾，是把采样范围收缩到「模型真正有信心的核」。
52	
53	注意函数的操作对象是**概率**（softmax 之后），不是 logits——核采样的定义就建立在「累积概率质量」上，logits 空间里没有对应物。
54	
55	#### 4.1.2 核心流程
56	
57	输入：`probas`，形状 `(batch, vocab_size)` 的概率分布（生成循环里传入的是 `(1, vocab)`，因为取了 `[:, -1]` 后仍保留 batch 维）；标量 `top_p`。
58	
59	```
60	top_p_filter(probas, top_p):
61	  0. 若 top_p 为 None 或 >= 1.0：原样返回（不过滤）
62	  1. 排序    sorted_probas, sorted_idx = 按概率降序排序（记下原位置）
63	  2. 累积和  cumprobas[j] = sorted_probas[0] + ... + sorted_probas[j]
64	  3. 选核    prefix[j] = cumprobas[j] - sorted_probas[j]   # 第 j 个 token 之前的质量
65	             keep[j]  = prefix[j] < top_p                   # 此前尚未攒够 top_p → 我属于核
66	             keep[0]  = True                                # 兜底：至少保留概率最大的 1 个
67	  4. 置零    核外 sorted_probas 置 0
68	  5. 回填    按 sorted_idx 把置零后的值散射回原始词表位置
69	  6. 重归一化 filtered / sum(filtered)，使每行重新和为 1
70	输出：与输入同形状、同「行列结构」的过滤后概率分布
71	```
72	
73	用规格里给定的例子手推一遍（这是本讲的核心算例，后面实践会验证）：
74	
75	排序后概率 \( p = (0.5,\ 0.41,\ 0.09) \)，取 \( \text{top\_p} = 0.9 \)。
76	
77	\[
78	\begin{aligned}
79	\text{cumprobas} &= (0.5,\ 0.91,\ 1.0) \\
80	\text{prefix} &= \text{cumprobas} - p = (0,\ 0.5,\ 0.91) \\
81	\text{keep} &= \text{prefix} < 0.9 = (\text{True},\ \text{True},\ \text{False})
82	\end{aligned}
83	\]
84	
85	保留前两个 token，保留质量 \( 0.5 + 0.41 = 0.91 \ge 0.9 \)——恰好是「累积质量**首次达到** 0.9 的最小集合」。重归一化后：
86	
87	\[
88	\left( \frac{0.5}{0.91},\ \frac{0.41}{0.91},\ 0 \right) \approx (0.5495,\ 0.4505,\ 0)
89	\]
90	
91	#### 4.1.3 源码精读
92	
93	**入口与短路分支**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L194-L196](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L194-L196)）：`top_p=None` 或 `top_p>=1.0` 时直接返回原张量——`top_p=1.0` 意味着「核 = 整个词表」，过滤是恒等操作，这一行短路既省计算又是文档（默认无过滤）。函数签名从这里也可看出它期望二维输入（下面所有操作都在 `dim=1` 即词表维上进行）。
94	
95	**Step 4.1 排序**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L198-L199](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L198-L199)）：`torch.sort(probas, dim=1, descending=True)` 同时返回排好序的值 `sorted_probas` 和「排序前每个值住在哪个词表位置」的索引 `sorted_idx`。后者是第 5 步回填的钥匙——概率必须回到它原来的词表 id 上，否则采样出的 token id 会张冠李戴。
96	
97	**Step 4.2 累积和**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L201-L202](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L201-L202)）：`torch.cumsum` 沿词表维做前缀和，得到每个排序位上的累积质量。
98	
99	**Step 4.3.1 前缀质量判据与兜底**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L204-L209](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L204-L209)）：

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 top_p_filter：五步流水线

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

`top_p_filter` 解决的问题：**在概率分布上动态划一条截止线，把长尾「核外」token 的概率清零，再把剩余质量重归一化为合法分布**，供后续 `torch.multinomial` 采样。

它和温度的分工可以用一句话概括：

> **温度负责「重塑」整个分布的形状，top-p 负责「砍掉」分布的尾巴。** 温度再怎么调，每个 token 的概率都还是正数；top-p 之后，核外 token 的概率严格为 0，永远不可能被采到。

为什么要砍尾巴？实践中发现（这正是原论文标题 "The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration" 指出的现象）：语言模型分布的长尾里堆满了语料中「偶尔出现过」的低质拼接，人类文本从来不会从均匀的全词表里选词。砍掉长尾，是把采样范围收缩到「模型真正有信心的核」。

注意函数的操作对象是**概率**（softmax 之后），不是 logits——核采样的定义就建立在「累积概率质量」上，logits 空间里没有对应物。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

输入：`probas`，形状 `(batch, vocab_size)` 的概率分布（生成循环里传入的是 `(1, vocab)`，因为取了 `[:, -1]` 后仍保留 batch 维）；标量 `top_p`。

```
top_p_filter(probas, top_p):
  0. 若 top_p 为 None 或 >= 1.0：原样返回（不过滤）
  1. 排序    sorted_probas, sorted_idx = 按概率降序排序（记下原位置）
  2. 累积和  cumprobas[j] = sorted_probas[0] + ... + sorted_probas[j]
  3. 选核    prefix[j] = cumprobas[j] - sorted_probas[j]   # 第 j 个 token 之前的质量
             keep[j]  = prefix[j] < top_p                   # 此前尚未攒够 top_p → 我属于核
             keep[0]  = True                                # 兜底：至少保留概率最大的 1 个
  4. 置零    核外 sorted_probas 置 0
  5. 回填    按 sorted_idx 把置零后的值散射回原始词表位置
  6. 重归一化 filtered / sum(filtered)，使每行重新和为 1
输出：与输入同形状、同「行列结构」的过滤后概率分布
```

用规格里给定的例子手推一遍（这是本讲的核心算例，后面实践会验证）：

排序后概率 \( p = (0.5,\ 0.41,\ 0.09) \)，取 \( \text{top\_p} = 0.9 \)。

\[
\begin{aligned}
\text{cumprobas} &= (0.5,\ 0.91,\ 1.0) \\
\text{prefix} &= \text{cumprobas} - p = (0,\ 0.5,\ 0.91) \\
\text{keep} &= \text{prefix} < 0.9 = (\text{True},\ \text{True},\ \text{False})
\end{aligned}
\]

保留前两个 token，保留质量 \( 0.5 + 0.41 = 0.91 \ge 0.9 \)——恰好是「累积质量**首次达到** 0.9 的最小集合」。重归一化后：

\[
\left( \frac{0.5}{0.91},\ \frac{0.41}{0.91},\ 0 \right) \approx (0.5495,\ 0.4505,\ 0)
\]

**入口与短路分支**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L194-L196](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L194-L196)）：`top_p=None` 或 `top_p>=1.0` 时直接返回原张量——`top_p=1.0` 意味着「核 = 整个词表」，过滤是恒等操作，这一行短路既省计算又是文档（默认无过滤）。函数签名从这里也可看出它期望二维输入（下面所有操作都在 `dim=1` 即词表维上进行）。

280	核采样的原始定义是：**保留最小的 token 集合，使其累积质量 ≥ top_p**。「最小集合」意味着：一个 token 属于核，当且仅当**在它之前的质量还没攒够 top_p**——一旦攒够了，后面的 token 就都多余了。
281	
282	源码把这句话直接翻译成了张量判据：
283	
284	\[
285	\text{keep}[j] \iff \underbrace{\sum_{i<j} p_{(i)}}_{\text{prefix}[j]} < \text{top\_p}
286	\]
287	
288	其中 \( p_{(i)} \) 是降序排列后的第 i 大概率。而 `cumprobas < top_p` 翻译的是另一句话：「连我算在内都没攒够」——它实现的是「保留质量**严格小于** top_p」，会在阈值被跨过的那一刻过早收手，丢掉跨阈值的那个 token。

393	## 6. 本讲小结
394	
395	- `top_p_filter` 是一条五步流水线：**排序 → 累积和 → 前缀质量判据选核 → 置零并回填原词表位置 → 重归一化**，作用于 softmax 之后的概率，输出仍是合法分布。
396	- 边界判据 `prefix < top_p` 精确翻译了核采样定义「累积质量首次达到 top_p 的最小集合」；写成 `cumprobas < top_p` 会丢掉跨阈值的 token，导致过度截断（算例：0.91 vs 0.5）。
397	- `keep[:, 0] = True` 是极端/非法 `top_p`（如 0 或负数）下的兜底，保证核非空，把崩溃降解为「退化为贪心」。
398	- `top_p=1.0` 或 `None` 走短路分支原样返回；极小 `top_p` 使分布坍缩为 one-hot，等价 argmax。
399	- `generate_text_top_p_stream_cache` 在温度采样三步（缩放→softmax→multinomial）中间插入过滤这一步，形成「logits 层调温、概率层砍尾」的分工；**`temperature=0` 时 top-p 完全被绕过**，这是实验中最常见的坑。
400	- 温度 + top-p 的组合（如 0.8 + 0.9）是仓库的标准采样配置，被 `self_consistency_vote` 消费，并被第 6 章 `sample_response` 原样复用——本讲的过滤器是全书推理时扩展与 RL 训练的公共零件。

核采样的原始定义是：**保留最小的 token 集合，使其累积质量 ≥ top_p**。「最小集合」意味着：一个 token 属于核，当且仅当**在它之前的质量还没攒够 top_p**——一旦攒够了，后面的 token 就都多余了。

源码把这句话直接翻译成了张量判据：

\[
\text{keep}[j] \iff \underbrace{\sum_{i<j} p_{(i)}}_{\text{prefix}[j]} < \text{top\_p}
\]

其中 \( p_{(i)} \) 是降序排列后的第 i 大概率。而 `cumprobas < top_p` 翻译的是另一句话：「连我算在内都没攒够」——它实现的是「保留质量**严格小于** top_p」，会在阈值被跨过的那一刻过早收手，丢掉跨阈值的那个 token。

至于 `keep[:, 0] = True`：`prefix[0] = 0`，只要 `top_p > 0`，`0 < top_p` 自然成立，这一行看似多余。它的真正职责是兜住**非正的 top_p**（例如误传 `top_p=0`）：此时所有 `prefix < 0` 全为 False，若没有这行强制保留，分布会全零，重归一化除以 `clamp_min(1e-12)` 后仍全零，`multinomial` 将报「invalid distribution」错。一行兜底把「非法参数」降解为「退化为贪心」的安全行为。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

三种判据在同一算例上的对比（`p = (0.5, 0.41, 0.09)`）：

| 判据 | keep | 保留质量 | 问题 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prefix < top_p`（源码，top_p=0.9） | (T, T, F) | **0.91 ≥ 0.9** ✓ | 无——恰好首次达到 0.9 |
| `cumprobas < top_p`（错误版） | (T, F, F) | 0.5 < 0.9 ✗ | 丢掉跨阈值 token，过度截断 |
| `cumprobas <= top_p`（另一错误版） | (T, F, F) | 0.5 < 0.9 ✗ | 本算例与 `<` 版同样过度截断；但换一组分布（如 `(0.5, 0.4, 0.1)`、`top_p=0.9`，cumprobas=(0.5, 0.9, 1.0)）它又碰巧给出 (T,T,F) 与源码一致——行为随「累积是否恰好等于 top_p」漂移，不可靠，见 4.3.5 练习 2 |

极端 `top_p` 的行为边界：

| top_p | 行为 | 对应源码 |
|---|---|---|
| `None` / `≥ 1.0` | 短路原样返回（恒等过滤） | L195-L196 |
| `0.001`（极小正数） | 核收缩到头名 token，输出退化为 one-hot `(1, 0, …, 0)`，采样等价贪心 | L207-L209 + L222 |
| `0` / 负数（非法） | `keep[:, 0]=True` 兜底，同样退化为 one-hot，不报错 | L209 |

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**判据与兜底三行**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L204-L209](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L204-L209)）：`prefix = cumprobas - sorted_probas` 用「累积和减去自身」优雅地算出「排在我之前的质量和」，避免再写一次累积；注释 "Example: [0.5, 0.41, 0.09] with top_p=0.9 should keep the first two tokens" 明确记录了边界意图——0.91 越过 0.9 的那个 token（0.41）被保留。`keep[:, 0] = True` 的注释 "(fallback for very small/non-positive top_p)" 直言其防御使命。

**严格小于的必要性**：若写成 `prefix <= top_p`，算例 `prefix = (0, 0.5, 0.91)`、`top_p=0.9` 下结果不变（0.91 > 0.9），但在「恰好等于」的边界上（如 4.1.5 练习 1 的 `prefix[2] = 0.6`、`top_p=0.6`）会多保留一个 token。严格 `<` 让「保留质量恰好等于 top_p」时果断收手，集合真正「最小」。

**下游对边界的依赖**：第 6 章 GRPO 的 `sample_response` 原样复用本函数（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py:L78](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py#L78)，导入见 L9）——rollout 采样同样依赖「核非空」这一兜底保证，否则一次误传参数就会让整个训练循环崩溃在 `multinomial` 上。

#### 4.3.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：用实验对比「正确判据」与「两种错误判据」的保留集合差异，直观理解边界含义。示例代码：

1. **操作步骤**：

```python
# 示例代码：三种判据的边界对比
import torch
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch04 import top_p_filter

def naive_filter(probas, top_p, mode):
    """复刻 top_p_filter，但分别用两种可疑判据。示例代码。"""
    sp, si = torch.sort(probas, dim=1, descending=True)
    cum = torch.cumsum(sp, dim=1)
    if mode == "prefix":       # 源码版
        keep = (cum - sp) < top_p
    elif mode == "cum_lt":     # 错误版：< 
        keep = cum < top_p
    keep[:, 0] = True
    kept = torch.where(keep, sp, torch.zeros_like(sp))
    out = torch.zeros_like(probas).scatter(1, si, kept)
    return out / out.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True).clamp_min(1e-12)

cases = [
    ([[0.5, 0.41, 0.09]], 0.9),
    ([[0.5, 0.4, 0.1]],   0.6),   # 测试用例：保留质量 0.9，留前两个
    ([[0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1]], 0.6),  # 恰好等于边界：prefix[2]=0.6
]
for p, tp in cases:
    p = torch.tensor(p)
    ref = top_p_filter(p, top_p=tp)
    bad = naive_filter(p, tp, "cum_lt")
    kept_ref = (ref > 0).sum().item()
    kept_bad = (bad > 0).sum().item()
    print(f"top_p={tp}: 源码保留 {kept_ref} 个, 错判据保留 {kept_bad} 个")
```

2. **需要观察的现象**：三个算例中错判据都比源码**少保留一个** token——丢掉的正是「跨过阈值」的那个：算例一、二里源码保留到累积质量越过 0.9/0.6 的 token，错判据在它前一位就停手；算例三里边界恰好取到精确值（`prefix[2] = 0.6` 恰等于 top_p），源码因严格 `<` 在此收手保留 2 个，错判据在 `cum[1] = 0.6` 处同样为 False，只保留 1 个。
3. **预期结果**：算例一：源码保留 2 个（0.5495/0.4505）、错判据保留 1 个（1.0）；算例二：源码保留 2 个（0.5556/0.4444，与 tests/test_ch04.py:L82-L91 的断言一致）、错判据保留 1 个；算例三：源码保留 2 个（0.5/0.5，保留质量恰为 0.6）、错判据保留 1 个。具体打印**待本地验证**。
4. 若想再探 `keep[:, 0]` 兜底，可在 `naive_filter` 里去掉那一行、传 `top_p=0.0`，观察输出全零——这就是兜底存在的理由。

#### 4.3.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：用一句话向同学解释 `prefix < top_p` 与 `cumprobas < top_p` 的区别。

**答案**：前者问「**轮到我之前**质量攒够 top_p 了吗？」——没攒够我就属于核，因此恰好保留「首次达到 top_p」的最小集合；后者问「**连我算上**攒够了吗？」——会在跨过阈值前一步提前收手，保留质量严格小于 top_p，过度截断。

**练习 2**：判据用 `cumprobas <= top_p`（把 `<` 换成 `<=`）在算例 `(0.5, 0.41, 0.09)`、`top_p=0.9` 下保留谁？在什么分布下它与源码版结果不同？

**答案**：`cumprobas = (0.5, 0.91, 1.0)`，`<= 0.9` 给出 `(T, F, F)`，只保留头名——比源码激进。关键在于它**不稳定**：源码判据 `prefix[j] < top_p` 等价于「前一位的累积和 `cum[j-1] < top_p`」，语义在任何输入下都一致；而 `cumprobas <= top_p` 只在「某位置累积**恰好等于** top_p」时才与源码碰巧重合（如 `(0.5, 0.4, 0.1)`、`top_p=0.9`：cumprobas=(0.5, 0.9, 1.0)，`<=` 给出 (T,T,F)，恰与源码相同），其余情形照旧丢掉跨阈值 token。边界行为随输入漂移的判据无法依赖，这正是源码选择把「严格小于」放在 prefix 上的理由。数值实验见 4.3.4 算例三（`(0.3, 0.3, 0.3, 0.1)`、`top_p=0.6`，两版一留二、一留一）。

**练习 3**：`denom.clamp_min(1e-12)`（L220）在什么情况下才真正派上用场？既然有 `keep[:, 0] = True`，它是不是死代码？

**答案**：仅在「所有概率被清零」时才有意义，而 `keep[:, 0] = True` 加上 softmax 输出恒正已经排除了这种情况（分母 ≥ 最大概率 > 0），所以对本函数的合法调用而言它是防御性冗余，不是死代码——它是纵深防御的一层：将来若有人改判据、传 NaN/全零张量或复用此函数到非 softmax 输入上，clamp 把「除零崩溃」降解为「输出极端值」，配合测试更容易暴露问题而非静默炸掉。

## 5. 综合实践

**任务：写一个「top-p 扫描器」，量化核大小与熵随 top_p 的变化。**

不带模型、纯 CPU 张量运算即可完成，把本讲三个模块串起来：

1. 构造三个「性格不同」的分布（示例代码）：
   - 尖峰型：`[0.9, 0.05, 0.03, 0.02]`（下一词几乎确定）
   - 平坦型：`[0.3, 0.28, 0.25, 0.17]`（下一步很开放）
   - 现实型：`[0.5, 0.41, 0.09]`（本讲算例）
2. 对每个分布，让 `top_p` 从 0.1 扫到 1.0（步长 0.1），逐档调用 `top_p_filter`，记录三列：**保留 token 数**、**过滤前保留质量**（重归一化之前的行和）、**过滤后分布的熵**。
3. 把结果整理成表，回答三个问题：
   - 同一 `top_p` 下，尖峰型与平坦型保留的 token 数差多少？（top-p 的自适应性）
   - 熵随 `top_p` 下降的速度，尖峰型和平坦型哪个更陡？为什么？
   - `top_p=1.0` 这一档走的是哪条分支（对照 [reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L195-L196](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L195-L196)），熵等于多少？
4. **预期结果**（手算可先行推出，程序验证待本地进行）：尖峰型在 `top_p=0.9` 时只保留 1 个 token（第 2 个的 prefix=0.9 不小于 0.9，熵为 0）；平坦型在 `top_p=0.9` 时保留**全部 4 个**（第 4 个 token 的 prefix=0.83 < 0.9，仍属核，熵不变）；现实型如正文，保留 2 个、熵约 0.689 nat——三种「性格」在同一 `top_p` 下的核大小截然不同，这正是 top-p 优于固定个数 top-k 的地方。

进阶（可选）：仿照 `count_samples`（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py:L132-L147](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch04.py#L132-L147)）对过滤后的分布各采样 1000 次，用频率分布复算熵，验证「采样频率 ≈ 概率」在核变小后收敛更快还是更慢。

## 6. 本讲小结

- `top_p_filter` 是一条五步流水线：**排序 → 累积和 → 前缀质量判据选核 → 置零并回填原词表位置 → 重归一化**，作用于 softmax 之后的概率，输出仍是合法分布。
- 边界判据 `prefix < top_p` 精确翻译了核采样定义「累积质量首次达到 top_p 的最小集合」；写成 `cumprobas < top_p` 会丢掉跨阈值的 token，导致过度截断（算例：0.91 vs 0.5）。
- `keep[:, 0] = True` 是极端/非法 `top_p`（如 0 或负数）下的兜底，保证核非空，把崩溃降解为「退化为贪心」。
- `top_p=1.0` 或 `None` 走短路分支原样返回；极小 `top_p` 使分布坍缩为 one-hot，等价 argmax。
- `generate_text_top_p_stream_cache` 在温度采样三步（缩放→softmax→multinomial）中间插入过滤这一步，形成「logits 层调温、概率层砍尾」的分工；**`temperature=0` 时 top-p 完全被绕过**，这是实验中最常见的坑。
- 温度 + top-p 的组合（如 0.8 + 0.9）是仓库的标准采样配置，被 `self_consistency_vote` 消费，并被第 6 章 `sample_response` 原样复用——本讲的过滤器是全书推理时扩展与 RL 训练的公共零件。

## 7. 下一步学习建议

- **u5-l3（思维链提示实验）**：换一个不采样的推理时扩展手段——只改提示模板、权重与采样参数都不动，对比两者「花钱买准确率」的方式有何不同。
- **u5-l4（自一致性投票）**：看 `generate_text_top_p_stream_cache`（`temperature=0.8, top_p=0.9`）采出的多条推理路径如何经 `extract_final_candidate`（u4-l2）提取短答案、再 `Counter` 投票定案——本讲的过滤器正是那里多样性与质量兼得的来源。
- **源码延伸**：提前翻一眼 [reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py:L78](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch06.py#L78)，确认 GRPO 的 rollout 采样循环与本讲 L252-L258 几乎逐行同构，为单元七热身。
- **理论延伸**：读 Holtzman 等人 2020 年的 *The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration*（本书第 4 章的参考之一），看人类文本的「核质量」统计如何支撑「只在核内采样」这一设计。

1. **解释**思维链（Chain-of-Thought, CoT）提示为什么能在**完全不碰权重、完全不用随机采样**的前提下，把 0.6B 基座模型在 MATH-500 上的准确率从 15.2% 拉到 40.6%。

4. **设计**属于自己的第三个提示模板变体，并在同一子集上做出「无提示 vs CoT vs 自设计」的三方对照实验。

## 2. 前置知识

本讲站在两块已建好的地基上，不再重复推导：

- **u4-l1（提示模板）**：`render_prompt` 把角色设定、`\boxed{ANSWER}` 输出契约、题干与作答起点 `Answer:` 拼成 zero-shot 提示；提示模板是评测协议的一部分，只改几个词就能让准确率大幅波动。
- **u4-l4（端到端评测）**：MATH-500 评测是「**渲染 → 生成 → 提取 → 判分**」四步链路，逐题写 jsonl 日志；生成环节占 99% 以上耗时。

同时回忆 u5-l1/u5-l2 的结论——温度与 top-p 是在**概率分布上动手脚**的采样手段。本讲恰好相反：**解码全程是贪心（确定性）的**，唯一的变量是拼进 prompt 的几个单词。这是三种推理时扩展手段中最便宜、也最「软」的一种。

本讲需要的新概念：

| 概念 | 一句话解释 |
|---|---|
| **思维链（CoT）** | Wei 等人 2022 年提出：让语言模型在给出最终答案前先生成中间推理步骤。直觉是——Transformer 每生成一个 token 只做「一层固定深度」的计算，复杂题一步算不出来；把推理展开成几十上百个 token，等于给了模型几十上百次串行计算的机会。 |
| **Zero-shot CoT 提示** | 不给示例（few-shot），只在提示末尾加一句「一步一步解释」之类的指令，诱导模型模仿预训练语料中大量存在的分步解题文体。本讲的后缀 `\n\nExplain step by step.` 就是经典写法（Kojima 等人 2022 年的 "Let's think step by step" 同源）。 |
| **推理时扩展（inference-time scaling）** | 不改权重，只在**推理阶段**花更多计算（更长的生成、更多次采样）换准确率。CoT 是其中最基本的一种：计算花在「单次回答更长」上。 |

## 4. 核心概念与源码讲解

### 4.1 CoT 提示模板：一行后缀的注入点

#### 4.1.1 概念说明

本讲的「CoT 提示模板」不是新模板，而是在第 3 章既有模板**末尾追加一个可配置后缀**。设计动机很实际：`render_prompt` 是全仓库共享的（第 3 章基线、本讲 CoT、第 4 章自一致性脚本都用它），如果为了 CoT 重写一个模板，就要复制维护两份几乎相同的字符串；而「基础模板 + 可选后缀」把变量收敛成一个参数——`prompt_suffix`。

这就是「对照实验」的正确姿势：**控制变量**。基线与 CoT 两次评测的唯一差别是那一个后缀字符串，模型、权重、解码方式（贪心）、数据集完全一致，准确率差异才能干净地归因到提示上。

#### 4.1.2 核心流程

```
render_prompt(problem)                     # 第 3 章模板，以 "Answer:" 结尾
        │
        ▼
prompt += prompt_suffix                    # ← 本讲唯一的注入点
        │        prompt_suffix = ""                      → 基线
        │        prompt_suffix = "\n\nExplain step by step."  → CoT
        ▼
generate_text_stream_concat(...)           # 贪心生成（KV 缓存版）
```

最终 prompt 的形态（以书中演示题为例）：

```text
You are a helpful math assistant.
Answer the question and write the final result on a new line as:
\boxed{ANSWER}

Question:
Half the value of $3x-9$ is $x+37$. What is the value of $x$?

Answer:

Explain step by step.
```

注意一个容易被忽略的细节：后缀拼接在**整个模板的最后**，也就是落在 `Answer:` 这个作答起点**之后**。最终的提示读起来是「……请作答：（换行）请一步步解释」——指令出现在作答区的开头，模型会把它当作作答要求的一部分。这不是笔误，而是零样本 CoT 的常见写法：指令紧贴生成起点，诱导效果最强。

书中 notebook 4.3 节用这道题做了单题对照（见 [ch04_main.ipynb](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/01_main-chapter-code/ch04_main.ipynb) 4.3 节）：

| 提示 | 模型输出（节选） | 提取结果 | 正误 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 基线（无后缀） | ` \boxed{20}`（几乎立刻报答案） | 20 | ✗（真值 83） |
| + `\n\nExplain step by step.` | 设方程 → 两边乘 2 → 移项 → `x = 83` → `\boxed{83}` | 83 | ✓ |

基线输出只有几个 token；CoT 输出是几百 token 的完整推导。这一行对照同时展示了本讲的**收益**（答对）与**代价**（变长）——代价在 4.3 节量化。

#### 4.1.3 源码精读

**基础模板**（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch03.py:L413-L420](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch03.py#L413-L420)）：`render_prompt` 用 f-string 把题干嵌进固定模板。注意 `\boxed{ANSWER}` 这行输出契约没有变——无论加不加 CoT 后缀，答案提取器 `get_last_boxed` 依然靠它锚定最终答案。**CoT 只改变「答案之前生成什么」，不改变「答案长什么样」**，所以下游提取与判分环节零改动。

**注入点**（[ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py:L45-L46](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py#L45-L46)）：评测循环里 `render_prompt(row["problem"])` 之后紧跟 `prompt += prompt_suffix`（源码用 `# NEW` 注释标记这是相对第 3 章版本的全部改动之一）。两行代码，就是「CoT 提示」在这个仓库里的全部实体。

**后缀从哪来**（[ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py:L127-L132](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py#L127-L132)）：`--prompt_suffix` 命令行参数，默认空串（即基线），help 文本直言用途 "Can be used to adds a chain-of-thought prompt"。README 第 8-12 行实验（[README.md:L148-L156](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/README.md#L148-L156)）示范了传入 `"\n\nExplain step by step."` 的写法。

**两处文本的细微出入**：notebook 4.3 节的拼接是 `prompt + " \n\nExplain step by step."`（`\n\n` 前多一个空格，因为模板以 `Answer:` 结尾、无尾随空格），而 README 与脚本的推荐用法是 `"\n\nExplain step by step."`（无前导空格）。差异只有一个空白字符，对分词与生成的影响可忽略，但做复现实验时值得知道两者并非逐字节相同。

#### 4.1.4 代码实践

**实践目标**：不跑模型，纯文本层面验证「后缀注入位置」与「模板不变性」。

1. **操作步骤**（示例代码）：

```python
# 示例代码：观察 prompt_suffix 的注入效果
from reasoning_from_scratch.ch03 import render_prompt, load_tokenizer_only

problem = "Compute 1/2 + 1/6."
base = render_prompt(problem)
cot = base + "\n\nExplain step by step."

print(repr(base[-20:]))   # 模板结尾长什么样
print(repr(cot[-45:]))    # 后缀接在哪里

tok = load_tokenizer_only("base")   # 只下载分词器，不碰权重
print("基线 prompt token 数:", len(tok.encode(base)))
print("CoT   prompt token 数:", len(tok.encode(cot)))
```

2. **需要观察的现象**：基线模板以 `"Answer:"` 结尾；后缀紧随其后；两个 prompt 的 token 数只差几个（后缀本身约 5-6 个 token）。
3. **预期结果**：`repr` 输出确认拼接位置在 `Answer:` 之后；CoT prompt 比基线长约 5-6 个 token。具体数值**待本地验证**（依赖分词器版本）。
4. 若把后缀换成 `" \n\nThink step by step."` 或 `"\n\nLet's think about this step by step."`，重新 encode 比较长度——这就是 4.3 节综合实践里「第三个模板变体」的预演。

#### 4.1.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：为什么不直接写一个 `render_prompt_cot(problem)` 新函数，而要搞「模板 + 后缀」？

**答案**：对照实验需要控制变量。`render_prompt` 被第 3 章基线、本讲脚本、自一致性脚本共用，如果为 CoT 复制一份模板字符串，两份模板日后一旦各自改动就会引入「模板漂移」——届时准确率差异无法归因是 CoT 还是模板本身变了。后缀方案把差异压缩到**一个字符串参数**上，基线就是 `prompt_suffix=""` 的特例，模板保持单一事实来源。

**练习 2**：CoT 后缀为什么放在 `Answer:` 之后而不是塞进开头的角色设定里？

**答案**：两个理由。其一，指令紧贴**生成起点**时，它直接构成模型第一个生成 token 的最近上下文，诱导效果最强；放在开头则可能被长题干「稀释」。其二，开头是角色设定区（"You are a helpful math assistant."），改动它等于改动第 3 章基线协议，破坏与基线的可比性——后缀方案保证不与基线共享的部分仅是追加的几个 token。

**练习 3**：CoT 让模型在 `\boxed{}` 之前生成几百个 token 的推导。从「每 token 计算量」角度解释这为什么可能提升准确率。

**答案**：Transformer 单次前向的计算深度是固定的（28 层），模型「想多久」不是由层数决定，而是由**生成多少个 token** 决定——每个新 token 都以全部前文为条件，等于多了一轮完整的网络计算。一道需要多步代数操作的题，指望一次前向算完相当于让模型「心算」；CoT 把中间结果逐个写进上下文，后续步骤可以「看着」前面的结果算，相当于把心算变成打草稿。

### 4.2 评测循环：复制-改造的 evaluate_math500_stream

#### 4.2.1 概念说明

`cot_prompting_math500.py` 里的 `evaluate_math500_stream` 不是从 `ch03` 导入的，而是把 [reasoning_from_scratch/ch03.py:L503-L574](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch03.py#L503-L574) 的同名函数**复制过来改了两处**。这是一种常见的工程取舍：库函数是给 notebook 用的稳定接口，而实验脚本需要快速加实验开关（`prompt_suffix`）；与其给库函数加一个只被一个脚本消费的参数，不如让脚本自带一份可随意魔改的评测循环。代价是两份代码需要人肉同步——比如第 3 章版本里有 `total_len` 平均响应长度统计（ch03.py:L519、L530），本脚本就没有带过来。

#### 4.2.2 核心流程

```
main (L141-L185)
  ├─ 解析参数：device / which_model / dataset_size / max_new_tokens
  │            / compile / prompt_suffix / verbose
  ├─ load_math500_test()                  # 500 题，本地缓存优先
  ├─ load_model_and_tokenizer(...)        # base 或 reasoning 权重
  ├─ model.eval() + TF32 精度设置
  └─ evaluate_math500_stream (L24-L92)
       for 每道题 (L44):
         1. render_prompt(problem) + prompt_suffix     L45-L46
         2. generate_text_stream_concat（贪心+KV缓存） L47-L51
         3. extract_final_candidate(gen_text)          L53-L55
         4. grade_answer(extracted, row["answer"])     L56-L59
         5. 写一行 jsonl 记录                          L61-L69
         6. 打印 ETA 进度                              L71-L78
       汇总：Accuracy、Total time、日志路径             L87-L92
```

#### 4.2.3 源码精读

**循环主体四步链路**（[ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py:L44-L59](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py#L44-L59)）：与 u4-l4 精读过的第 3 章版本逐行对应——渲染（含后缀）、生成、提取、判分；`num_correct += int(is_correct)` 累计对题数。生成调用的 `generate_text_stream_concat`（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch03.py:L121-L145](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch03.py#L121-L145)）内部消费的是 `generate_text_basic_stream_cache`（[reasoning_from_scratch/ch02.py:L117-L142](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/reasoning_from_scratch/ch02.py#L117-L142)）——贪心 argmax 解码，**没有任何温度或 top-p**。这一点决定了本讲实验的解读方式：所有差异只能来自 prompt。

**jsonl 记录**（[ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py:L61-L69](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py#L61-L69)）：每题写一行七字段 JSON——`index / problem / gtruth_answer / generated_text / extracted / correct` 加文件句柄。`generated_text` 保留完整推导过程，是事后分析「模型怎么想的」的原始材料；`ensure_ascii=False` 让 LaTeX 原文可读。

**命令行参数**（[ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py:L95-L138](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py#L95-L138)）：

| 参数 | 默认 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| `--device` | `auto` | `auto` 走 `get_device()` 自动探测，否则接受任意 torch 设备串 |
| `--which_model` | `base` | `base` / `reasoning` / `instruct` 三选一（见下方映射） |
| `--dataset_size` | `10` | 取 MATH-500 **前 N 题**做子集评测——快速实验的旋钮 |
| `--max_new_tokens` | `2048` | 生成上限。默认给到 2048 正是为 CoT 长推理留空间（第 3 章版本默认 512） |
| `--compile` | 关 | 开启 `torch.compile`（见 u3-l3） |
| `--prompt_suffix` | `""` | **本讲主角**：空串即基线，传 CoT 后缀即实验组 |
| `--verbose` | 关 | 逐题打印提取结果与当前对题数 |

**instruct 变体映射**（[ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py:L160-L171](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py#L160-L171)）：命令行的 `instruct` 并没有对应的第三套权重——它被映射为 `reasoning` 权重，但在加载后追加一行 `tokenizer.add_thinking = False`。回忆 u2-l6：`add_thinking` 决定聊天模板是否预填一个空的 `<think>` 块；关掉它，reasoning 模型就被当成「不带思考标签的指令模型」用。这是用现有两套权重模拟第三种模型形态的小技巧。

**评测调用**（[ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py:L176-L185](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py#L176-L185)）：`math_data[:dataset_size]` 切片控制规模，`out_path` 用 f-string 拼成 `math500_{模型}-{设备}-evaluate-script.jsonl`。**注意：文件名里没有 prompt_suffix 的信息**——先后跑基线和 CoT 两次，第二次会覆盖第一次的日志（综合实践中会处理这个问题）。

#### 4.2.5 小练习与答案

**练习 1**：脚本的 `evaluate_math500_stream` 相对 `ch03.py` 原版改了什么、删了什么？

**答案**：改了两处——函数签名新增 `prompt_suffix=""` 参数（L32），循环内 `render_prompt` 之后追加 `prompt += prompt_suffix`（L46），两处都带 `# NEW` 注释。删了一处——第 3 章版本的 `total_len` 累计与「Average response length」输出（ch03.py:L519、L530、L571-L572）没被带过来。其余（四步链路、jsonl 字段、ETA 进度、汇总打印）逐行一致。

**练习 2**：`--dataset_size 10` 是随机抽 10 题吗？这样做对照实验有什么隐患？

**答案**：不是随机——`math_data[:dataset_size]` 取的是数据集**前 10 题**（顺序切片）。隐患有二：其一，MATH-500 的题目按类型/难度分布未必均匀，前 10 题可能是同类题，子集准确率对方差极大；其二，10 题的准确率粒度是 10%，单题翻转就是 10 个百分点。结论方向可信、具体数字不可信——正式结论应以全量 500 题为准（README 表格即是）。

**练习 3**：为什么这个脚本的 `--max_new_tokens` 默认值（2048）比第 3 章评测函数的默认值（512）大？

**答案**：因为 CoT 模式下模型要先生成完整推导再给 `\boxed{}`，几百到上千 token 是常态；若上限太紧，生成会在推出答案**之前**被截断，`extract_final_candidate` 只能回退到「全文最后一个数字」，把中间量当最终答案，判分几乎必错——截断把「会做但没说完」误伤成「做错」。预填给足空间是 CoT 实验的隐性成本之一（更长的生成 = 更久的时间）。

### 4.3 结果统计：收益、代价与基准解读

#### 4.3.1 概念说明

推理时扩展没有免费的午餐：**准确率的每一分提升都用推理计算量买来**。CoT 的账本尤其清晰——它买准确率的方式是「把一次回答变长」，因此代价直接体现在生成 token 数与评测时长上。读基准表格时要同时看两列：Accuracy 和 Time。

#### 4.3.2 核心流程

来自 README（全量 500 题、DGX Spark GPU 上的实测，[README.md:L39-L46](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/README.md#L39-L46)）：

| 行 | 方法 | 模型 | 准确率 | 耗时 | 相对基线 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 基线（第 3 章，贪心） | Base | 15.2% | 10.1 min | — |
| 2 | 基线（第 3 章，贪心） | Reasoning | 48.2% | 182.1 min | 权重不同，不可比 |
| 3 | **CoT 提示** | Base | **40.6%** | **84.5 min** | 准确率 ×2.67，耗时 ×8.37 |

收益与代价的换算：

\[
\text{准确率增幅} = \frac{40.6 - 15.2}{15.2} \approx 167\%,\qquad
\text{耗时增幅} = \frac{84.5 - 10.1}{10.1} \approx 737\%
\]

耗时多 8 倍多的直接原因：基线模式下模型常常几个 token 就报出 `\boxed{20}` 然后停在 EOS；CoT 模式下每题要生成几百 token 推导。生成耗时近似正比于生成 token 数，所以「时间倍率 ≈ 平均回答长度倍率」。

再看组合实验（同表 L83-L97，[README.md:L83-L97](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/README.md#L83-L97)）里一个反直觉的数据点：

| 行 | 方法 | 准确率 |
|---|---|---|
| 3 | CoT（贪心） | 40.6% |
| 8 | Top-p 采样 + CoT | 33.4% |
| 11 | 自一致性(n=10) + Top-p + CoT | 52.0% |

把 u5-l1/u5-l2 的采样（temperature 0.9 + top_p 0.9）叠上去，0.6B base 上不升反降（40.6% → 33.4%）——小模型的单次采样推理链方差太大，一条链走偏就全错；直到用 10 次采样投票（第 11 行，52.0%）才把多样性转化回准确率。这条「CoT → CoT+采样 → CoT+采样+投票」的递进链正是 u5-l4 的内容。

#### 4.3.3 源码精读

**运行命令**（[README.md:L49-L62](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/README.md#L49-L62)）：README 给出的是全量 500 题命令 `python cot_prompting_math500.py --which_model "base" --dataset_size 500`——注意它**没有传 `--prompt_suffix`**，复现表格第 3 行的 CoT 结果需要自行追加 `--prompt_suffix "\n\nExplain step by step."`（同文件 L148-L156 的第 8 行命令里有示范）。README 同时注明（L45、L98）：表内数字是 DGX Spark（CUDA）全量 500 题实测，换硬件绝对时间不可比，准确率在同种子贪心解码下可复现。

**汇总输出**（[ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py:L87-L92](https://github.com/rasbt/reasoning-from-scratch/blob/b8646024377b0a35b44eddd2ec506c1a63f1b791/ch04/02_math500-inference-scaling-scripts/cot_prompting_math500.py#L87-L92)）：循环结束后打印准确率（对题数/总题数）、总耗时（分钟）与日志路径，并把三元组 `(num_correct, num_examples, acc)` 返回给调用方。配合 `--verbose`（L79-L85）可在评测中逐题查看 `Extracted / Expected / Correct so far`。
